title_prefix: VerifyDB never runs at startup and verif
mechanism: Two halves, both confirmed. (a) No startup call site: sb-introspect:who-calls on bl.rpc::rpc-verifychain returns only the two tests in tests/rpc/rpc-tests.lisp and tests/validation/reorg-tests.lisp (plus this session's probes); nothing in src/node/init.lisp reaches it, and -checkblocks / -checklevel are registered as :core-only, i.e. accepted and dropped (src/config-options.lisp:438, confirmed live: config-option-kind returns :CORE-ONLY for both). Core runs CVerifyDB().VerifyDB over EVERY non-empty chainstate on every boot inside VerifyLoadedChainstate, with -checkblocks default 6 and -checklevel default 3, and turns CORRUPTED_BLOCK_DB into a hard startup failure, _("Corrupted block database detected") (refs/bitcoin/src/node/chainstate.cpp:240-276, refs/bitcoin/src/validation.h:77-78). (b) The RPC stops at Core's level 1: rpc-verifychain (src/rpc/blockchain.lisp:775-806) walks the last nblocks entries, reads each block back (level 0) and, at checklevel >= 1, re-checks the merkle root and proof of work -- and then stops. It never opens an undo record (Core level 2, validation.cpp:4703-4712), never constructs a coins view over the coins DB and DisconnectBlock's the tail against it (level 3, validation.cpp:4713-4733, which begins with assert(coins.GetBestBlock() == pindex->GetBlockHash())), and never reconnects (level 4, validation.cpp:4747-4769). checklevel is also not clamped to [0,4] as Core clamps it (validation.cpp:4659), so any value >= 1 is level 1. Levels 2-4 -- the ones that compare the block database against the UTXO set -- exist nowhere in the tree.
consequence: A chainstate that disagrees with its blocks is never detected, at startup or on demand, and the RPC that exists to detect it answers true. Executed on a real regtest chain with real proof of work and a LevelDB-backed coins view: at height 8 with 8 coins, verifychain with NO arguments (checklevel 3, nblocks 6) returned T; after coins-view-cache-wipe left the UTXO set at 0 coins while the tip, the block index and every blk/rev record stayed in place -- the state confirmed S1 bbf6e679 produces after its 'Recovered' log line -- the same call still returned T, as did checklevel 4 and checklevel 99. The positive control (remove the tip block's body so level 0 must fail) returned JSON false, so the probe is not vacuous. Core's level-3 pass on that state DisconnectBlocks the last six blocks against the coins cache; with an empty view SpendCoin fails for every output, DisconnectBlock returns DISCONNECT_UNCLEAN, pindexFailure is set and VerifyDB returns CORRUPTED_BLOCK_DB, so Core refuses to start where we start and report success. The same absence covers torn undo records, a rev file lost with its blk file, and a coins DB restored from a mismatched backup: all go unreported until a reorg or a spend hits them. S2 rather than S3 because an operator acts on the answer -- a default-level verifychain reporting true is the assurance a node runner uses before returning a node to service, and it is wrong by three of Core's four levels; S2 rather than S1 because this is a missing detector, not itself a wrong write.
evidence: Probes under build/ga11v/p3b.lisp and build/ga11v/p3c-verifydb-regtest.lisp, run with scripts/dev.sh eval on the project container in worktree bl-ga11v-storage-s2. (1) ga11v-p3c on a regtest node built from regtest-node-fixture with a LevelDB coins-view-cache and undo storage, 8 blocks mined via rpc-generatetodescriptor "raw(51)": (:BEFORE (:HEIGHT 8 :COINS 8 :VERIFYCHAIN-DEFAULT T :VERIFYCHAIN-LEVEL-4 T) :AFTER-WIPE (:COINS-AFTER-WIPE 0 :HEIGHT 8 :VERIFYCHAIN-DEFAULT T :VERIFYCHAIN-LEVEL-4 T :VERIFYCHAIN-LEVEL-99 T) :POSITIVE-CONTROL-MISSING-BODY YASON:FALSE). (2) Caller sweep in the image: (:WHO-CALLS 13) resolving to the two shipped tests plus this session's probe functions only; (:CHECKBLOCKS-KIND :CORE-ONLY :CHECKLEVEL-KIND :CORE-ONLY). (3) Tree grep for checkblocks/checklevel/verifychain/VerifyDB over src/ and tests/ finds the option table, the RPC, its two tests and the Core tables -- no startup path. Ours: src/rpc/blockchain.lisp:775-806; src/config-options.lisp:438; src/node/init.lisp (no call site). Core at d3056bc: refs/bitcoin/src/node/chainstate.cpp:240-276; refs/bitcoin/src/validation.cpp:4643-4775; refs/bitcoin/src/validation.h:77-78.
fix_shape: Do not implement here. Two separable pieces, both close to Core. First, finish the RPC: give rpc-verifychain Core's levels, clamping checklevel to [0,4] as validation.cpp:4659 does and walking the tail from the tip -- level 2 reads each block's undo record through the same reader the disconnect path uses and fails on a read error, level 3 builds a scratch coins view over the chainstate's own coins DB, asserts its best-block equals the block being disconnected, and disconnects each block into it, treating an unclean disconnect as Core's pindexFailure (a false answer, not an exception), and level 4 reconnects back to the tip. Core's prune / snapshot-chainstate escape (validation.cpp:4684-4690: stop at the first block with no data instead of failing) and its cache-size guard (skipped_l3_checks when the coins usage would exceed the tip cache budget, validation.cpp:4716-4732) must come across too, or a pruned node will report corruption for missing history. Second, wire it into startup: move -checkblocks and -checklevel off the core-only list into the known-config-options table with Core's defaults 6 and 3, and call the verifier from %init-recover-chain over every chainstate once the block index and coins view are open, refusing to start on the corrupted result the way load-header-index's third case already refuses -- that is the half that turns bbf6e679's state from 'runs and reports success' into Core's 'Corrupted block database detected'. Note the option move is not free: an option that leaves the accept-and-drop list must be added to the known table in the same change or start-up fails with Invalid parameter.
